summary: Implemented settings.merge.merge per ADR-004 (recursive dict merge, lists and other values replaced, None removes a key, no mutation of inputs via deep copies) and added tests covering each rule plus load(). All 6 tests pass.
assumptions: A None override for a key absent from base is a no-op (key stays absent).
When an override dict replaces a non-dict base value, it is merged into an empty dict so None entries inside it are also dropped, keeping None-means-unset consistent at every depth.
Results are deep-copied so later mutation of the result cannot affect cached input layers.
